subject: Phased model cutover: comms runway & customer exemption catalog
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@acme.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Beth Carlson <beth.carlson@enterprisesolutions.com>
Date: 2024-05-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Phased cutover questions + exemptions for Acme pilot

Hi Maya — thanks for the note earlier. A couple quick asks from our side as we scope the pilot: 1) can you share the types of exemptions you typically allow (e.g., longer TTL on legacy endpoints, variant pinning, regional egress exceptions)? 2) what's a realistic communications runway we should expect (how many weeks / what level of notice for a pinned-variant deprecation)?

We want to prepare our internal stakeholders — legal and platform engineering — and Beth is helping coordinate the procurement side. If you have a one-pager or a canonical list, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Samir
--
Samir Desai
Head of AI Platform, Acme Corp
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@acme.com>
Cc: Beth Carlson <beth.carlson@enterprisesolutions.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-17T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Phased cutover questions + exemptions for Acme pilot

Thanks Samir — good questions. Putting a short summary below and looping in our cross-functional leads to confirm operational constraints and the comms template. Attaching a draft matrix and an exemption CSV for your review.

High-level answers: 
- Typical exemption categories: variant pinning (customer-specific model hash), extended read-only grace windows (up to 30 days for critical endpoints), egress-location waivers (for regulated data, region-limited fallbacks), and temporary QoS guarantees (burst reservation for migration cutover).
- Default runway: 4–6 weeks for public deprecations (announced to all customers), 2–3 weeks for targeted phased migrations (pilot customers & partners) — exceptions possible with a documented approval and rollback plan.

Notes / asks: 
- Marissa: can you confirm comms cadence / templates and whether we will require a weekly status update to customers during the runway?
- Mateo: can you validate scheduling assumptions for dedicated pools during the 2–3 week pilot cutover?
- Karthik / Infra: we may need an escape hatch for disabled KV cache behavior — what's the impact/effort?

Attachments: phased-cutover-matrix.xlsx (matrix of gates + owners), customer-exemption-catalog.csv (example).

Thanks — I will consolidate responses and send a single runway proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@acme.com>
Cc: Beth Carlson <beth.carlson@enterprisesolutions.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-17T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Phased cutover questions + exemptions for Acme pilot

+1 on the summary. Operational comms notes: 
- We use a three-touch cadence for pilots: initial notice (owner + technical impact), two-week reminder with migration checklist, and a 48-hour pre-cutover readiness check. All touches are templated but tailored per-account.
- For exempted customers we maintain a special comms lane: weekly status email + opt-in rollback window.
- I will own the public email templates; attaching runway-comm-template.md for feedback.

Action: Maya — if you want customer-specific wording, send me the impacted endpoints and the exact variant pins. Samir — if Acme needs a longer notice window, tell us target weeks and I will map to the three-touch cadence.

Marissa
Director, Customer Ops
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-18T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Phased cutover questions + exemptions for Acme pilot

Quick scheduling constraints and capacity notes: 
- For a 2–3 week pilot cutover we can reserve a dedicated pool but need a confirmed start date at least 10 business days before cutover to provision and run soak tests.
- If Acme opts for variant pinning, expect KV cache warm-up impact on first 24–48 hours post-cutover; recommend a 48-hour monitoring window with elevated logging.
- Attachment \"phased-cutover-matrix.xlsx\" (row highlights) updated with estimated lead times.

Ask: Samir — can you confirm a preferred start week by next Tue (2024-05-21) so we can lock capacity?

-Mateo
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-19T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Phased cutover questions + exemptions for Acme pilot

Technical clarifications on exemptions / gating: 
- Variant pinning: supported, but only for specific model families and quantization profiles. Pin request must include model hash + inference profile. We can support up to 5 pinned variants per account without extra engineering work; beyond that we need a scoped SOW.
- Egress / region waivers: supported for Private customers; for hosted accounts we can route to a regional variant but may require contractual egress addendum.
- Soft-landing: we can enable transparent fallback to a compatibility variant for 72 hours post-cutover. This requires a short-lived routing policy and increased quota for the fallback pool.

Risk notes: prolonged pinning extends our testing burden and will be prioritized lower in the deprecation schedule unless tied to an active contract.

Irene — can you confirm approval flow for contract-level egress waivers?

Karthik
Senior Staff, Inference Engineering
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-20T15:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Phased cutover questions + exemptions for Acme pilot

Confirming approval flow and next steps: 
- Contract-level egress waivers and atypical SLAs require VP legal approval plus Product leadership sign-off. I will own the routing to Legal and escalate as needed.
- For this pilot: if Acme requests any contract changes (egress, extended pinning beyond 30 days), we require a signed amendment and a security review. 

Next steps / owners: 
- Maya: consolidate runway proposal and finalize customer wording (EOD 2024-05-20) — include the exact endpoints & variant hashes.
- Marissa: finalize comms templates and weekly status cadence; prepare a sample 48-hour readiness checklist.
- Mateo: lock capacity after Samir confirms week; run soak tests.
- Karthik: prepare technical flyer on pinning limits & soft-landing mechanics for the customer.
- Priyom: once runway is consolidated, I need a single decision doc to route to Legal for any contract-level exceptions.

I will start the legal intake if Maya flags contract ask in the final doc.

Irene Choi
VP, Product & Compliance
